definitions.explanation: An undesirable situation or outcome that someone ends up in, typically as a result of their own actions or circumstances beyond their control. Almost always used in the pattern 〜する{羽目|はめ}になる.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}り{遅|おく}れて、{歩|ある}く{羽目|はめ}になった。
examples.english: I missed the train and ended up having to walk.

examples.japanese: {約束|やくそく}を{忘|わす}れて、{謝|あやま}る{羽目|はめ}になった。
examples.english: I forgot my promise and ended up having to apologize.

examples.japanese: {安|やす}いからと{飛|と}びついたら、{修理|しゅうり}{代|だい}で{余計|よけい}に{払|はら}う{羽目|はめ}になった。
examples.english: I jumped at it because it was cheap, but ended up paying even more in repair costs.

notes:
USAGE:
{羽目|はめ} is almost exclusively used in the pattern 〜する{羽目|はめ}になる (to end up having to ~), expressing an undesirable outcome. It always carries a negative nuance — the speaker did not want this result.

KEY PATTERN:
- verb (dictionary form) + {羽目|はめ}になる (to end up having to ~)
- {払|はら}う{羽目|はめ}になる (to end up having to pay)
- {待|ま}つ{羽目|はめ}になる (to end up having to wait)
- やり{直|なお}す{羽目|はめ}になる (to end up having to redo it)

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- 〜する{羽目|はめ}になる: emphasizes the undesirable result
- 〜するはめになる: same meaning (sometimes written without kanji)
- 〜ざるを{得|え}ない: "have no choice but to" (more formal, less focus on misfortune)
